requiredFindings.problem: The selectionLaw insertion says the core provider closure is never selected otherwise, explicitly included. The same successor's IE:1377 insertion, M3-C r7 item 9, and README row 5 say it is never selected otherwise, not even explicitly. The parent selectionLaw already allows extra retained closures to be selected explicitly, so the schema sentence withdraws that permission in the wrong direction.
requiredFindings.evidence: IE1377_ADD (build_crc_1.py lines 152-156) and the IE:1377 after end with: and is never selected otherwise, not even explicitly; the core adapter closure is never a semanticClosures member. SELECTION_ADD and the selectionLaw after end with: and is never selected otherwise, explicitly included; the core adapter closure is never a member. README.md row 5 says the pointer appends the same exception as row 2. M3-C r7 item 9 (PROPOSAL-r7.md:443) makes the core provider a plan.semanticClosures member exactly when a syntax universe is selected, and never otherwise. C2-T13 (PROPOSAL-r7.md:470) refuses the closure in semanticClosures when no syntax universe is selected, and refuses its absence when one is selected. check_crc_1.py checks needles in the IE:285 paragraph and does not compare the selectionLaw after with that exception, so both rev checks passed with this sentence in place.
requiredFindings.fix: In SELECTION_ADD, replace the words otherwise, explicitly included with otherwise, not even explicitly. The selectionLaw after becomes: Direct members must be in plan.semanticClosures. Other-input dependencies need not be flattened into it; extra admissible retained closures may be selected explicitly. There is no exact-minimal-set constraint. The core role closures are the exception (contract successor CRC-1): the core provider closure is a direct member exactly when the Plan selects a native.semantic-universe.syntax.v2 universe, and is never selected otherwise, not even explicitly; the core adapter closure is never a member. Regenerate successor.json, PASSAGES.md, and crc-1-subject.json from the builder. In check_crc_1.py, after the IE:285 needle loop, assert that this after contains never selected otherwise, not even explicitly and does not contain explicitly included.

nonBlockingObservations.observation: The pinned SYN-1F draft identity-schemas.v3.json is 198763 bytes, sha256 6583540f31afbcb017b089075630105d0fbf8eb013c5d8618a2d1a0b01600af3. The live unbound file is 200510 bytes, sha256 694389668d89cc99f1fd64b0460a565dd4b0ef88b2831472307da9c1568438ae. Its three CRC-1 strings are IDS-L's strings plus the current CRC-1 appends, including the selectionLaw sentence in RF-1. README's statement that the draft leaves the three strings identical to IDS-L describes the pinned draft. The absorb-whichever-binds-second procedure remains the right coordination. At bind time the live draft's befores are the appended strings, and after RF-1 that draft has to take the corrected selectionLaw sentence if it keeps the premature copy.

build_crc_1.py --check rebuilds every subject file to the same bytes and differs only on crc-1-unit.json, which is outside the subject. The single line difference is the review path: the builder emits docs/implementation/m3/reviews/codex-crc-1-r1/review.json and the draft records docs/implementation/m3/reviews/grok2-crc-1-r1/review.json.
